priorities: ROI first: the goal is affiliate income. The homepage quiz drives most Amazon clicks, so send readers into the quiz, ideally at their type (https://hairtypequiz.hair/?type=4C).
Pinterest is the biggest channel after direct visits: 1-3 pins a day, each linking to a post or the quiz.
Near-page-1 pages earn the fastest gains: better titles and intros for searches at Google positions 8-16.
Evidence-led: cite PubMed for any claim, mark untested claims "not studied".

facts: On average African hair grew more slowly than Caucasian hair: 256 vs 396 micrometres a day, about 3.7 vs 5.7 inches a year (Loussouarn 2001, PMID 11531795); a 2016 study of 2,249 adults agreed (PMID 27019510). Both group people by ethnicity, not curl type.
Tightly coiled hair knots in 10-16% of shafts vs 0.15% in other groups (Khumalo 2000, PMID 11050586).
Combing damage rises with every stroke; 480 strokes did more cuticle damage than frequent braiding (PMID 33605448).
Coconut oil gets into the hair shaft and reduced protein loss as a pure oil before and after washing (PMIDs 11413497, 12715094); it was not tested inside styling creams.
No study compares curl creams, and none shows a cream reduces shrinkage; stretching comes from styling and drying methods.
Aunt Jackie's Curl La La contains no flaxseed (the brand's Don't Shrink gel does).
avoid: Star ratings, review counts, Amazon prices or "Amazon's #1 / bestseller" claims (removed site-wide Oct 28).
Saying Strand tested products; it doesn't.
Invented numbers, studies, PMIDs or percentages (e.g. shrinkage percentages).
Cure, growth-guarantee or health claims; in Meta ads, "you/your hair" personal framing.
Promising any lead magnet other than the 4C Wash Day Checklist.
rules: Plain-words affiliate disclosure before the first Amazon link; Amazon tag strand01-20.
Palette: espresso #3D2B1F, caramel #C4945A, cream #FAF7F2; text on light backgrounds uses #8B5E1A.
Pins: 1000x1500, keyword in the first 40 characters of the title, straight apostrophes, footer hairtypequiz.hair.

pins: Every pin links to a post or the quiz; quiz pins by hair type earn the most clicks.
Titles up to 100 characters, keyword first; descriptions up to 500, no hashtag stuffing.
outline: Lead the title with the exact search phrase; meta 140-155 characters; answer the question in the first two sentences.
Plan a quiz link and 2-3 internal links.
factcheck: Check every number against Verified facts; anything else is unverified, with a PubMed search phrase to settle it.
compliance: FTC: disclosure before the first affiliate link. Amazon: the required statement is in every footer; no prices or ratings.
visual: The owner prefers Canva photographic pins: real natural hair, no before/after, warm light.
critique: Check the footer is spelled hairtypequiz.hair, look for AI flaws in hands and hair, and check headline readability at phone size.
custom: Strand is hairtypequiz.hair: a free hair type quiz (1A-4C) plus an evidence-led blog, paid by Amazon affiliate clicks.
